summary: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 is a careful extraction of Gan–Ichino, The Shimura–Waldspurger correspondence for Mp_2n (Ann. of Math. 188 (2018)). After its review it has 104 items (1 library, 21 planned, 82 missing), 6 routes and 7 source issues. Its statements match the published text. The one library claim holds at the pins. E4–E7 check out, including E7, the counterexample to Jiang–Soudry Th. 2.2(2) that makes Proposition A.2 unproved as printed for n ≥ 2. The rejections of E1–E3 are right. There are 12 findings: 6 medium and 6 low. (1) Route 2 puts into MP.3 items stated with the Part II's own constructions (parabolic induction on the cover and χ_ψ, the ψ-relative parameter, the Π_{φ,ψ} labelling), so the parent depends on its Part II. The extraction contradicts itself by planning Kudla's filtration, which needs the same preimages P̃, at MP.3. (2) The global functional equation and root numbers of GL_m, and the ε-compatibility of the local Langlands correspondence, have no item, although Lemma 4.3, and through it ε_φ and Lemmas 6.8–6.12, rest on them. The complete L-functions L(1/2, Φ) and L_ψ(s, Π) are never defined. (3) selfdual-types and partial-l-function stay 'planned' although the review found no stage plans ∧²/Sym² L-functions or the exponent bound that E5 needs; they are not routed. (4) The unitarity of π_{φ_v} (Corollary 4.2, citing Tadić) has no item; the atlas owner is ET.6 through Jiang–Zhang 20. (5) Weak containment and Fell isolation, and the Sakellaridis–Venkatesh Poincaré-series theorem, are also routed by Gan–Savin 23-B to SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitaryDual and LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2. (6) The p-adic Langlands quotient theorem has three owners (SR.3 via Gan–Savin 23, the doubling Part II, and this Part II for covers). Low: (7) the Rallis inner product formula and its Siegel–Weil input are named, never stated; (8) strong multiplicity one has two further owners besides AL.3; (9) the MVW involution and Li's stable-range non-vanishing each have a second owner; (10) Ishimoto's Th. 3.14(2) proves both parts of (6.1), settling the review's open question; (11) an unrecorded citation gap at p. 1004 (Prasad–Schulze-Pillot's lemma does not cover S_0); (12) no sourceVersions.

Disclosure. This session red-teamed PAPER-DOR-23 (PR #4815; its finding /5 is about the Weil representation in positive characteristic and a MetaplecticAutomorphicForms extension) and PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21 (PR #4740; its finding /5 is about owners of the real Langlands classification). Finding 2 touches AF.1b only in noting the archimedean ε-compatibility, and does not rely on it. Finding 6 is about the p-adic Langlands classification, not the real one. Versions. The published Annals text (annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v188-n3-p05-s.pdf, 52 pages, pp. 965–1016) was read in full through pdftotext on 30 September 2026. Its SHA-256 be54266f…87d68c0 reproduces the extraction's. Printed pp. 975 and 1003 were rendered as images, confirming the complex conjugates the review added. arXiv 1705.10106v3 (SHA-256 5d1408c5…b291d, reproduced) was compared at every passage used, including reference [44] (E4 confirmed). The arXiv listing shows v1–v3, with v3 the latest. Crossref records no update-to or relation for doi 10.4007/annals.2018.188.3.5. Ishimoto arXiv:2301.12143v2 was read at its introduction, Theorems 3.11–3.14 and §5.1.

The whole paper was read: §1 (Theorem 1.1, Remarks 1.2–1.3, §1.2 local Shimura, Theorem 1.4, Remark 1.5, Corollary 1.6, §1.4 idea of proof, §1.5 endoscopy); Notation; §2 (Mp_2n, quadratic spaces and ε(V), theta lifts, the conservation relation, abstract and automorphic lifts, Kudla–Rallis Cor. 7.1.3, rank, (2.2), the global rank equivalence, Theorem 2.1); §3 (Proposition 3.1 with (3.1)–(3.3), Remarks 3.2–3.3); §4 (Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2 with (4.3)–(4.4), (4.5), Lemma 4.3, Proposition 4.4, Remark 4.5); §5 (L-parameters, (5.1)–(5.3), Lemmas 5.1–5.2, Remark 5.3, (5.6), Proposition 5.4, Lemma 5.5); §6 (Proposition 6.1, Lemmas 6.2–6.4, (6.1), Propositions 6.5–6.6, Corollary 6.7, Lemmas 6.8–6.12 with (6.2)–(6.6)); Appendix A (Propositions A.1–A.4, the Whittaker and relative Poincaré series, (A.1)–(A.2)); and the references.

All 104 items were read against the paper: statement, locator, status, planned stages and library citations, together with the extraction's notes and the review's notes. Counts: 1 library, 21 planned, 82 missing. Every missing item is routed exactly once, and check_paper.py reports ok. The following statements were re-derived: the pole and 'largest t' argument of Proposition 3.1 with E5; Lemma 4.3's sign computation (including orthogonality of Sym² Std_i and Std_i ⊠ Std_j); the ψ_a-twist of Remark 1.3; the proofs of Lemmas 6.8, 6.10, 6.11 (including the real case) and 6.12; Corollary 6.7's non-goodness and injectivity; the Hasse-sign counterexample (−1, −1)^{r(r−1)/2} on H^r ⊕ ⟨1⟩ over Q_2; and the Krasner construction in rev-number-fields-with-prescribed-completions.

All seven source issues were checked at their locators. E1–E3 were rejected by the review, and I agree. For E1, Gan–Savin's argument needs only −s + t_1 ≠ (k − r)/2. For E2, Adams–Barbasch Th. 8.4 plus Kudla cover the case. For E3, Ichino–Lapid–Mao state the Mp analogue. E4 is confirmed: the published [44] is the Märchen, while v3's [44] is 'On the notion of an automorphic representation'. E5 is confirmed: the pole needs L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0. E6 is confirmed. E7 is confirmed through the conservation relation. A σ′^{−ε} first occurring at Mp_2n gives a ψ-generic supercuspidal whose lift is not supercuspidal. This is consistent with ILM's cuspidality hypothesis in Prop. A.7, and the Proposition A.1 descents satisfy the corrected hypothesis. I then looked for missed issues across the paper and found one (finding 11).

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 route 2 (source → MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.3): items induction-principle, mvw-involution, unramified-theta, rev-unramified-theta-correspondence-from-mp, rev-dependence-of-theta-lifts-on; against route 1 (part-ii MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger): items metaplectic-induction, rmk-5-3, llc-mp, prop-6-1; and the planned item kudla-filtration (MP.3)
findings.claim: The parent layer MP.3 is made to depend on its own Part II. Route 1's Part II takes MetaplecticAutomorphicForms as parent and its brief says 'Import from: Metaplectic groups ... MP.0–MP.6'. But five items that route 2 puts into MP.3 are stated with constructions that route 1 places in the Part II. (i) induction-principle and mvw-involution are statements about Ind_{P̃}^{Mp_2n}(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0), with P̃ the preimage of a parabolic, M̃ = G̃L_k ×_{μ2} Mp_2n0 and τ̃_ψ = τ ⊗ χ_ψ. Those objects are item metaplectic-induction, which is 'missing' and routed to the Part II (route 1). unramified-theta is stated through the principal series (5.5) Ind_{B̃}(χ_ψ|·|^{s_1} ⊗ ⋯), also metaplectic-induction. (ii) unramified-theta ('the L-parameter ϕ of π relative to ψ') and rev-unramified-theta-correspondence-from-mp ('the L-parameter of π relative to ψ is ϕ_{θ_ψ(π)} ⊕ ...') use the ψ-relative parameter, which is defined in rmk-5-3 (route 1). (iii) rev-dependence-of-theta-lifts-on asserts 'Π_{φ,ψ_{a²}}(Mp_2n) = Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) with the same labelling π_η, and Proposition 6.1 for ψ is the same statement as for ψ_{a²}' (llc-mp and prop-6-1, route 1), and also a global statement (a character Ψ of F\A with prescribed square classes) that no local layer can hold. The extraction is also inconsistent with itself: kudla-filtration is marked planned at MP.3 ('Jacquet filtrations') although its statement needs 'P̃(X_r) ⊂ Mp(W) ... the preimage of the stabilizer of an r-dimensional isotropic X_r', the same preimages that metaplectic-induction says MP.3 does not plan. A Part II must start where its parent stops (PROTOCOL §15), so the MP.3 blueprint could not state these items without importing a later roadmap.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL.md §15: 'the additions form a roadmap that extends the existing one ... with the existing roadmap as its first prerequisite. It starts where the existing roadmap stops'. PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18.result.json, item metaplectic-induction, note: 'MP.3 plans the splitting characters of dual pairs but not parabolic subgroups of the cover or χ_ψ' and review note 'Route 1 should build them on top of SR.2 and MP.2'; routes[0].items contains metaplectic-induction and rmk-5-3; routes[1].items contains induction-principle, mvw-involution, unramified-theta, rev-dependence-of-theta-lifts-on and rev-unramified-theta-correspondence-from-mp. Statements quoted above are from those items. MP.3 stage text (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.json): 'Prove the splitting statements with the required auxiliary characters ... Prove the elementary equivariance, admissibility/finite-length statements in the source's range, see-saw identities, Jacquet filtrations and the explicitly needed first-occurrence/vanishing comparisons.' Source: the character χ_ψ of the cover of GL_k is 'given in [20, §2.6]' (p. 988), a Weil-index character, and Kudla's filtration is 'see, e.g., [24, Prop. 7.3]' (p. 988), stated on parabolic subgroups of Mp(W).
findings.fix: Move metaplectic-induction from route 1 to route 2 (MP.3), split into its local part (P̃, M̃ = G̃L_{k_1} ×_{μ2} ⋯ ×_{μ2} Mp_2n0, the description of genuine irreducible representations of M̃, χ_ψ built from MP.2's Weil index, and normalized induction on the cover on top of SR.2), which MP.3 needs for its Jacquet filtrations anyway, and its adelic part (P̃(A), the global χ_ψ and Ind_{P̃(A)}), which goes with MP.4–MP.5's genuine Eisenstein spaces or stays in route 1. Restate unramified-theta and rev-unramified-theta-correspondence-from-mp with Satake data only (unramified subquotient of (5.5) with exponents s_i ↦ unramified representation of SO(V) with the stated exponents), and let rmk-5-3 (route 1) define the ψ-relative parameter from them. Update the route-2 reason and the route-1 brief ('This extraction routes ... to MP.3'), and re-run check_paper.py.

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18: no item; items llc-gln-padic, llc-gln-arch, lemma-4-3, global-component-group, rev-epsilon-dichotomy-and-coherence, rallis-inner-product (b), prop-a-1
findings.claim: The global functional equation and root numbers of the standard L-function of GL_m, and the compatibility of the local Langlands correspondence for GL_m with ε-factors, are used but stated by no item. (a) Lemma 4.3 identifies Arthur's Galois-side product ε(s, φ, Std_i) = ∏_v ε(s, Std_i ∘ φ_v, ψ_v) with the automorphic root number ε(s, φ_i). That needs the local correspondence to carry Godement–Jacquet ε-factors to Weil–Deligne ε-factors at every place, archimedean ones included. llc-gln-padic and llc-gln-arch state only the bijection and the square-integrable/tempered dictionary. (b) Lemma 4.3's second assertion, which Lemmas 6.8, 6.11 and 6.12 use, deduces ε(1/2, φ_i) = 1 from L(1/2, φ_i) ≠ 0. That is the functional equation L(s, φ_i) = ε(s, φ_i) L(1 − s, φ_i) of the complete L-function of a self-dual cuspidal φ_i, with ε(1/2, φ_i) ∈ {±1} and L(s, φ_i) entire (n_i ≥ 2). rev-epsilon-dichotomy-and-coherence uses the same step ('ε(1/2, Φ) = 1, which holds because L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0'). (c) The complete L-functions L(1/2, Φ) (Proposition 6.5, Corollary 6.7) and L_ψ(s, Π) of a genuine automorphic representation (proof of Proposition A.1: 'L(1/2, T) = L(1/2, Σ) = L_ψ(1/2, Π) ≠ 0') are never defined: partial-l-function defines only L^S_ψ. The atlas plans (a) at p-adic places in ET.6 and (b) in AL.2, so the correct statuses are 'planned' with citations, plus missing items for the archimedean ε-compatibility and for L_ψ(s, Π).
findings.evidence: Published p. 983 (proof of Lemma 4.3): 'Since Std_i is symplectic and ε(s, φ, Std_i) = ε(s, φ_i), this implies the first assertion. If L(1/2, φ) ≠ 0, then since L(1/2, φ) = ∏_i L(1/2, φ_i), we have L(1/2, φ_i) ≠ 0 and hence ε(1/2, φ_i) = 1 for all i.' p. 982: ε(s, φ, ρ_j) = ∏_v ε(s, ρ_j ∘ φ_v, ψ_v). p. 970: 'ε_φ(a_i) = ε(1/2, φ_i), where ε(1/2, φ_i) ∈ {±1} is the root number of φ_i.' p. 1002: 'L(1/2, T) = L(1/2, Σ) = L_ψ(1/2, Π) ≠ 0', 'where L_ψ(s, Π) is the L-function of Π relative to ψ'. ET.6 stage text: 'Verify compatibility with ... L/epsilon factors' and 'irreducibility/bijectivity, and L/epsilon-factor compatibility'. AL.2 stage text: 'Build the adelic global integral for cuspidal GL_n representations, prove Euler factorization, analytic continuation and functional equation'. A search of the 104 items for 'functional equation', 'root number' and 'ε-factor' finds only local-shimura (preservation of ε-factors by θ_ψ) and rev-epsilon-dichotomy-and-coherence, neither of which states these facts.
findings.fix: Add a planned item 'global functional equation and root numbers for GL_m' citing AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.2: for cuspidal τ of GL_m(A), L(s, τ) = ε(s, τ) L(1 − s, τ^∨) with ε(s, τ) = ∏_v ε(s, τ_v, ψ_v) independent of ψ, L entire for m ≥ 2; hence for self-dual τ, ε(1/2, τ) ∈ {±1}, and L(1/2, τ) ≠ 0 forces ε(1/2, τ) = 1. Extend llc-gln-padic's statement with preservation of L- and ε-factors of pairs (planned, ET.6), and llc-gln-arch's with the archimedean ε-compatibility (missing, route 5). Add a route-1 item defining the complete L_ψ(s, Π) = ∏_v L(s, ϕ_{Π_v, ψ_v}) with the archimedean and ramified local factors of llc-mp, and its equality with L(s, Σ) under θ (local-shimura) as used in Proposition A.1. List these as prerequisites of lemma-4-3, rev-epsilon-dichotomy-and-coherence, rallis-inner-product and prop-a-1. Disclosure: the archimedean ε-factors are among the targets that FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 proposes for a new stage AF.1b; this finding does not depend on that proposal, and route 5's target is left as it is.

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 items selfdual-types (status planned, ML.4) and partial-l-function (status planned, AL.4)
findings.claim: Two items keep status 'planned' although the review's own evidence shows that the stages named do not plan them. Nothing routes them. (1) selfdual-types: the exterior- and symmetric-square L-functions, their poles and Shahidi's non-vanishing at s = 1, and the dichotomy 'exactly one of L(s, φ_i, ∧²), L(s, φ_i, Sym²) has a pole'. The review wrote 'Recommend status missing, routed as a source to ML.4 (route 3)' but left the status unchanged, so ML.4's blueprint is not told to plan them. (2) partial-l-function: its second sentence, holomorphy of L^S_ψ(s, π) for Re s > n + 1 for π in L²_disc(Mp_2n). After the confirmed E5, what the proof needs is absolute convergence (so non-vanishing) there, which requires a uniform bound on the Satake exponents of unitary unramified genuine representations. AL.4 proves convergence only 'where a supplied eigenvalue bound ensures it', and nothing supplies the bound. The review recommended splitting this off as missing under route 1, but did not. Because both items are 'planned', no design or blueprint job receives them.

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18: no item; items cor-4-2 and rmk-5-3
findings.claim: The unitarity of the unramified genuine representation π_{φ_v} with ψ_v-parameter φ_v, for φ a generic elliptic A-parameter, has no item. Corollary 4.2 needs it to apply Li's bijection (2.2), which is between unitary representations, and so to show that every σ in L²_{φ′}(SO_2r+1) has rank 2n. The paper cites Tadić's classification of the unitary dual of GL_n [86] together with Remark 5.3. rmk-5-3 states only the Lapid–Muić–Tadić criterion (each s_i ∈ √−1R, or s_i real with |s_i| < 1/2). The review observed that this criterion does not cover the exponents that occur, x ± iy with 0 < x < 1/2 and y ∉ {0, π/log q_v}, or x + πi/log q_v. It put the argument in a note, not in an item. So no layer plans the step. The atlas does have an owner for the input. PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (accepted) routes 'The generic unitary dual of GL_n over p-adic fields' (Tadić) to EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6.
findings.evidence: Published p. 980 (proof of Corollary 4.2): 'where π_{φ_v} is the irreducible genuine unramified representation of Mp_2n(F_v) whose L-parameter (relative to ψ_v) is φ_v. Note that such π_{φ_v} is unitary (see [86] and Remark 5.3 below). As explained in Section 2.3, such σ_v is of rank 2n'. p. 989 (Remark 5.3): 'by [46, Lemma 3.3], the representation (5.5) is unitary if either s_i ∈ √−1R or s_i ∈ R with |s_i| < 1/2 for all i.' [86] (p. 1015) is Tadić, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 19 (1986). rmk-5-3 review note: 'the unramified parameters of local components of unitary cuspidal φ_i can have exponents of the form it ± x (0 < x < 1/2), or x + πi/log q. The remark's criterion ... does not cover these literally. Unitarity then follows from Tadić's classification [86] together with unitary induction through G̃L_2 blocks'. PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20.result.json item tadic-unitary-dual, route 5 (source, ET.6), review verdict accept. Check of the case analysis: the multiset {±s_i} of a local component of a unitary symplectic φ_i is stable under s ↦ −s and s ↦ −s̄. A quadruple ±x ± iy therefore gives Ind from G̃L_2 of χ_ψ ⊗ (|det|^{iy} ⊗ the complementary series of GL_2 with exponent x < 1/2), which is unitary. Real s and purely imaginary s are covered by the Lapid–Muić–Tadić lemma.

findings.claim: Two pieces of abstract harmonic analysis have three proposed owners. (1) Weak containment and isolation in the Fell topology. GI's rev-whittaker-plancherel-support-and-weak (iii) says: if an irreducible unitary π_S is weakly contained in ⊕_i Π_i, then π_S lies in the Fell closure of {Π_{i,S}}, and if it is isolated, then π_S ≅ Π_{i,S} for some i. GI routes this to its Part II. Gan–Savin 23-B routes the same statements, Definition 11.5, Proposition 11.6 and Corollary 11.7, to SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitaryDual, 'stated also for finite products of such groups with compact groups, as the globalisation arguments use them'. (2) The Sakellaridis–Venkatesh Poincaré-series theorem (weak containment of the local L² space in the automorphic spectrum, through ⟨R_y P_f, P_f⟩ = ⟨R_y f, f⟩). GI's rev-whittaker-poincare-series-on-mp and (ii) route it to the GI Part II. Gan–Savin 23-B item 91 routes it to the new LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2, whose statement already covers the Whittaker case by citing GI. Both extractions and both reviews were accepted on 23 September, and neither mentions the other. The Gan–Savin Part II is limited to split simple p-adic groups, which excludes Mp_2n(F_S), the group GI needs.

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 item rallis-inner-product; route 1 brief, layer (4)
findings.claim: The Rallis inner product formula itself is stated nowhere, and neither are its inputs. The item lists four consequences, (a)–(d), and its note says 'The paper does not state the formula itself.' The route-1 brief names it only as '(Kudla–Rallis, Gan–Qiu–Takeda, Yamana)'. The consequences rest on three things. (1) The formula for (Mp_2n, O(V)) with dim V = 2n + 1, both directions, with its normalization: the partial value L^S_Ψ(1/2, Π) times the local doubling zeta integrals. (2) The non-vanishing of those local integrals exactly when the local theta lift is non-zero. (3) The regularized Siegel–Weil formula that proves it; the titles of [43] and [23] are 'A regularized Siegel–Weil formula'. A design job reading the brief would have to recover all this from the sources.
findings.evidence: rallis-inner-product note: '(a) is in the proof of Lemma 6.8, (b) in the proof of Proposition A.1, (c) in the proof of Lemma 6.10, and (d) in §1.4 ... The paper does not state the formula itself.' Review note on it: 'no stage plans the Rallis inner product formula or the regularized Siegel–Weil formula (searched)'. Published p. 997: 'Hence, by the Rallis inner product formula [43], [23], [93] and the local Shimura correspondence [2], [3], [24], there exists a unique V such that Θ^aut_{V,Ψ}(V) is nonzero'. References p. 1010: [23] 'The regularized Siegel-Weil formula (the second term identity) and the Rallis inner product formula'; p. 1012: [43] 'A regularized Siegel-Weil formula: the first term identity'.
findings.fix: Add to rallis-inner-product (or as a separate route-1 item) the formula in the form used: for cuspidal Π of Mp_2n(A) and dim V = 2n + 1, ⟨θ(f_1, ϕ_1), θ(f_2, ϕ_2)⟩ = c · L^S_Ψ(1/2, Π) · ∏_{v∈S} Z_v(f_{1,v}, f_{2,v}, ϕ_{1,v}, ϕ_{2,v}), with the constant and measures taken from [23]/[93]; the local non-vanishing criterion (Z_v ≢ 0 iff θ_{Ψ_v}(Π_v) ≠ 0 on V_v); the SO(V) → Mp_2n direction used in Lemma 6.10; and the regularized Siegel–Weil formula [43], [23] as a named prerequisite. In the brief, say that layer (4) owns the general regularized Siegel–Weil formula and the formula itself. Disclosure: FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 (this session, finding /19) already proposes that this Part II own the general regularized Siegel–Weil formula and the Rallis inner product formula, importing MP.6's binary and ternary instances. This finding agrees with that proposal but rests on the extraction and the paper alone.

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 item amf-nonsplit (review note); route 1 brief ('Corrections from the review', fourth bullet)
findings.claim: The review left open whether Ishimoto proves part (i) of the hypothesis, the decomposition of L²_disc(SO(V)) into near-equivalence classes for non-split SO(V). Lemma 6.10 needs it on Levi factors. The brief records only that 'Ishimoto's published result is confirmed for generic parameters only.' Ishimoto answers the question. His main theorem, Theorem 3.14(2), proves the decomposition, Theorem 3.12, for every inner form of SO_2n+1 over a number field and every parameter. It proves the multiplicity formula, Theorem 3.13, for generic parameters. Both parts of (6.1) as GI use them are therefore theorems, once Ishimoto's labelling of the packets is matched with the bijection (5.3) that GI take from Mœglin–Renard. Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.6 are then unconditional. The conditional wording in the brief would make the design job carry an open hypothesis that is no longer open.
findings.evidence: Ishimoto, arXiv:2301.12143v2 (read 30 September 2026, sha256 76cbb46c…aa58), Theorem 3.14: '2. Let F be global. Then Theorem 3.12 holds. Let moreover ψ = φ ∈ Φ(G*) be a generic parameter. Then Theorem 3.13 holds true for φ.' Theorem 3.12: 'There exists a decomposition L²_disc(G(F)\G(A_F)) = ⊕_{ψ∈Ψ(G*)} L²_disc,ψ(G(F)\G(A_F)), where L²_disc,ψ is a full near equivalence class of irreducible representations π = ⊗_v π_v in the discrete spectrum such that the L-parameter of π_v is φ_{ψ_v} for almost all v' (proved in §5.1: 'Theorem 3.12 is now proven.'). Introduction: 'the result of Gan-Ichino [10] on the generic part of AMF will be unconditional.' amf-nonsplit review note: 'Before Theorem 1.4 is recorded as unconditional, check whether Ishimoto also supplies (i) for the classes met in the cuspidality step of Lemma 6.10'.
findings.fix: In amf-nonsplit's note, replace the open check with: '(i) is Ishimoto Th. 3.12, proved for every non-quasi-split odd SO in Th. 3.14(2); (ii) is Th. 3.13 for generic parameters (Th. 3.14(2))'. In the brief's fourth correction bullet, say that both parts are Ishimoto's theorems, and route them to ML.4 as proved inputs, not hypotheses. The one remaining obligation is to match Ishimoto's packet labelling with (5.3). The scope is arXiv v2; the IMRN text was not read.

findings.where: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 sourceIssues (a missed gap in the proof of Proposition A.2, p. 1004); items psp-lemma and prop-a-2
findings.claim: A citation in the proof of Proposition A.2 does not cover every place it is applied to, and the gap is not recorded. The proof chooses f_v = P_v f̃_v for all v ∉ S_∞ ∪ S and normalizes '⟨f_v, f_v⟩ = 1', citing Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, Lemma 4.4. That lemma needs a supercuspidal representation, so it gives P_v f̃_v ≠ 0 only at v_0. At the unramified places the non-vanishing is a direct computation. At v ∈ S_0, however, f̃_v is a wave packet in a principal-series Bernstein component, and P_v f̃_v ≠ 0 needs a separate argument: the component consists of irreducible principal series, which are ψ_v-generic, so some element of its Hecke algebra has non-zero Whittaker projection. The review described this in the psp-lemma note but recorded no source issue. It is a gap that is easily filled, and it affects the proof only.
findings.evidence: Published p. 1004: '• if v ∈ S_0, then f̃_v belongs to the wave packet associated to a Bernstein component consisting only of irreducible principal series representations ... By [70, Lemma 4.4], we may further assume that ⟨f_v, f_v⟩ = 1.' [70] is Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, J. reine angew. Math. 616 (p. 1014). psp-lemma review text: 'Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, Lemma 4.4 ... is stated for ... a supercuspidal π; the integral converges only because matrix coefficients are compactly supported mod Z ... At v ∈ S_0 in A.2 the f̃_v are wave packets, not supercuspidal matrix coefficients. There, the nonvanishing of P_v f̃_v comes instead from the ψ_v-genericity of the irreducible principal series in the Bernstein component'. PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18.result.json sourceIssues E1–E7 contain no entry at p. 1004.
findings.fix: Add a source issue E8: kind gap, locator 'proof of Proposition A.2, p. 1004 (arXiv v3 p. 31)', printed text as quoted, correction 'at v ∈ S_0 choose f̃_v in the Hecke algebra of the principal-series component with P_v f̃_v ≠ 0, which exists because the component's irreducible members are ψ_v-generic (Whittaker functionals are non-zero on the component's summand of C_c^∞(G_v)); [70, Lemma 4.4] is needed only at v_0', affects 'the proof', known 'new' with the searches already listed.
